observed_text: A slab of thickness d adds a phase 2π(n−1)d/λ relative to vacuum, proportional to d. No thickness marks a beginning of refraction.
implied_text: Hardware is a polarizable bound-charge volume and a path through it; the output grows with the material traversed. Vacuum (N=0) and X-ray δ→0 are the low-contrast end of the same resource.
description: Refraction has no minimum thickness. The phase accumulates in proportion to (n−1) times the path.
notes: The first version contrasted this with a 10–20 nm metal-mirror floor, which does not exist. Reflection and refraction now agree that the output scales with the thickness traversed.

observed_text: Optical period λ/c is 1.50 fs at 450 nm, 1.83 fs at 550 nm and 2.17 fs at 650 nm. Water has a static dielectric constant of 80.10 at 20 °C and an optical permittivity n² = 1.7778.
implied_text: The bound-charge population must track the optical cycle. Channels slower than the drive fall out of the synchronized response. Drive well above the electronic resonances leaves n≈1.
description: Visible electronic refraction completes on a 1.5–2.2 fs cycle; a slower polarization channel is already off the clock.
notes: Water is the split-channel example: static 80.10 (20 °C) against optical 1.7778. The assignment of the difference to orientational polarization was not checked against an opened source.

observed_text: Zero continuous power and no stored directional state. Dielectric strength from a handbook compilation: air 3 MV/m; solids from 9.8–13.8 MV/m (window glass) to 470–670 MV/m (fused silica) and 2000 MV/m (diamond). Breakdown ends the insulating window.
implied_text: Driven collective response, not a memory. The high-field edge is a different machine class (dielectric-breakdown), not a sharper location of n.
description: Refraction has an operating window, not an energy barrier that stores a written state.
value_text: no latch; Ebd is a different family
notes: Cross-cite dielectric-breakdown. Do not file breakdown as the refraction cliff. The strengths rest on a tertiary page; the first version gave solids as 1e7–1e8 V/m.

observed_text: Above the electronic response the index is n = 1 − δ, with δ = n_e r_e λ²/2π in the free-electron limit: Si 5.4e-5 at 3 keV, 7.4e-6 at 8.05 keV, 1.2e-6 at 20 keV; water 2.6e-5, 3.6e-6, 5.8e-7. Vacuum is N = 0. n1 = n2 gives no interface kink.
implied_text: ε→1 (X-ray, vacuum, or drive above the electronic response) removes the contrast continuously and the ray kink fades.
description: The spectral and density failure is n−1→0, a crossover that goes as δ ∝ n_e λ².
value_text: δ ~ 1e-6–1e-5 at about 8–20 keV (light solids); n−1→0
notes: value_si is the geometric mean of the quoted δ decade. The first version placed that decade at a few keV. The δ values are this file's free-electron estimate. X-ray n<1 grazing total external reflection is the same kinematic gate as TIR with inverted contrast; geometry owned by total-internal-reflection. Free-electron analogue is plasma-frequency-cutoff.

observed_text: The phase 2π(n−1)d/λ is proportional to the path d. A path much shorter than λ gives a fringe-level shift, not a resolvable ray.
implied_text: A short path gives a proportionally small output. 'A wavelength or more' is a convention for calling the result a ray.
description: A short path is a continuous reduction of the ray output, not a missing polarizable volume.

observed_text: At 589.3 nm, from fitted dispersion formulas: water (20.0 °C) 1.33335; fused silica 1.45840; N-BK7 crown glass 1.51673; diamond 2.4173; standard dry air 1.000277. Optical permittivity is n².
implied_text: A stable, material- and frequency-specific n(ω) and the macroscopic Snell kink from synchronized bound-charge polarization.
description: The synchronized bound-charge population emits a tabulated n(ω) and a ray bend.
notes: value_si is N-BK7 crown glass. total-internal-reflection is the geometry/index gate on this same n.

observed_text: The dielectric itself draws no continuous power.
implied_text: Hold-power of the refracting slab is zero; the drive is the incident field.
description: Continuous draw to hold n is zero.

observed_text: Clausius–Mossotti / Lorentz–Lorenz relate (ε_r−1)/(ε_r+2) and (n²−1)/(n²+2) to Nα. They do not derive α from node rules. No thickness is measured at which refraction appears.
implied_text: QSA takes tabulated n(ω) and the X-ray δ as the contrast specification.
description: Contrast is located as Nα but α is not derived. That is a gap, not a contradiction.
notes: File-level mapping remains Medium. No source for the two relations was opened in the 2026-11 pass.

observed_text: δ = √(ρ/(π f μ0 μr)) is the 1/e depth of an exponential profile with a phase lag of one radian per δ. Copper at 293 K (pure 1.678e-8 Ω·m to IACS 1.7241e-8 Ω·m): 8.4–8.5 mm at 60 Hz; 2.1 mm at 1 kHz; 65–66 μm at 1 MHz; 2.1 μm at 1 GHz.
implied_text: The buffer is the screening length δ, quoted at 1/e by convention. There is no minimum thickness: a conductor of half-thickness a shows a surface-to-centre contrast that grows with a/δ.
description: Skin hardware is thickness against δ(ω), a 1/e length. The same metal is millimetres at power frequency and micrometres at radio frequency.
value_text: δ = 8.4–8.5 mm (Cu, 60 Hz) … 2.1 μm (1 GHz); 1/e depth
notes: value_si is 60 Hz in pure copper; IACS copper gives 8.53 mm. Optical λ/4πk (Ag 12.8 nm, Al 6.6 nm as intensity depths) is owned by reflection; London λ by meissner. A single pulse and a moving contact have their own depths (see the clock row). Do not collapse the lengths.

observed_text: Magnetic diffusivity D = ρ/μ0 is 0.0137 m²/s in IACS copper. Steady drive: δ ∝ f^(−1/2). Single pulse of length t: 2√(Dt) in the railgun literature and 0.8–2 times √(Dt) across rules (0.093–0.23 mm at 1 μs, 0.93–2.3 mm at 100 μs, 1.3–6.2 mm at 0.2–0.7 ms). Moving contact of length a at speed V: 2√(Da/V), which is 0.73 mm at 100 m/s and 0.33 mm at 500 m/s for a = 1 mm. The same electrons have a plasma period of 0.28–0.46 fs.
implied_text: The low-frequency clock is magnetic diffusion across the conductor, set by measured ρ and μ. One diffusivity is read against three drive clocks: period, elapsed time and transit time.
description: Skin is the same screening machine as reflection, run in the magnetic-diffusion band rather than on the plasma period.
value_text: 60 Hz class (power); δ ∝ f^(−1/2); pulse depth ∝ √(Dt) with D = 0.0137 m²/s (Cu)
notes: Cross-cite reflection (optical plasma period) and plasma-frequency-cutoff (high-frequency end). 60 Hz is an operating point, not a clock threshold. The pulse prefactor is a convention; the moving-contact depth is model-only, with no direct measurement found.

observed_text: The metal requires no auxiliary power beyond the current itself.
implied_text: Driven dissipative response, not a latch and not a gapped condensate. No static barrier holds the current distribution.
description: Skin has an operating window on ω and thickness, not an energy barrier that stores a written state.
notes: Meissner replaces this dissipative layer with a static London depth — different family.

observed_text: δ ∝ ω^(−1/2) grows without limit as ω → 0, and when δ is large against the conductor the current distribution is that of steady conduction. A factor of ten in frequency changes δ by a factor of about 3.
implied_text: Drive slower than the diffusion clock of the conductor → the surface-to-centre contrast fades continuously. There is no critical frequency.
description: The low-frequency collapse is uniform fill, reached continuously. Same machine as reflection, failed by a too-slow clock rather than a too-fast one.
notes: Twin of plasma-frequency-cutoff: that entry owns ω>ωp; this entry owns ω→0. The scale is δ = a.

observed_text: Field and current density fall as e^(−x/δ). A conductor whose half-thickness a ≪ δ carries current over its whole cross-section; a wire much thicker than δ has about the resistance of a tube of wall δ. At 4δ the amplitude is 1.8 % of the surface value.
implied_text: Spatial under-provisioning relative to δ: the responding population occupies the entire cross-section and the surface-to-centre contrast is absent.
description: The spatial twin of reflection’s thin-film limit, written against classical δ rather than optical λ/4πk. A crossover in a/δ.
notes: At 60 Hz in Cu the comparison length is 8.4–8.5 mm; at 1 GHz it is 2.1 μm. Cross-cite reflection for the optical thin-film limit.

observed_text: The local relation J = σE fails when δ falls below the mean free path ℓ. Copper at 293 K: ℓ = 39–40 nm against δ = 3.56 μm at 340 MHz (ratio 91) and 1.0–2.5 mm at 0.7–4 kHz; δ would equal ℓ only near 3 THz. In the extreme limit the surface resistance goes from ω^(1/2) to ω^(2/3).
implied_text: Mean-free-path over-run takes the machine out of the classical-δ specification into a different operating length. It is not reached in room-temperature copper below the terahertz range.
description: Anomalous skin is a local-response failure of the classical buffer, approached continuously in ℓ/δ.
value_text: ℓ ≳ δ; Cu at 293 K: ℓ = 39–40 nm
notes: The δ ∝ ω^(−1/3) scaling is inferred from the surface-resistance exponent; no opened source states it. Cold copper with a residual resistivity ratio near 100 has ℓ of about 4 μm. Pippard (1947) and Reuter and Sondheimer (1948) were not opened. Keep classical, anomalous and optical lengths distinct.

observed_text: AC current density is highest at the surface and falls as e^(−x/δ); a wire much thicker than δ has about the resistance of a hollow tube of wall δ carrying direct current. Neighbouring conductors redistribute the current further (proximity effect).
implied_text: Frequency-dependent concentration of AC current toward the surface, and the associated rise in AC resistance, from collective screening.
description: The synchronized electron gas emits an exponentially screened interior and a current sheet of 1/e depth δ.
notes: cyclotron-resonance (Azbel'–Kaner) uses this skin layer as the volume the microwave field occupies.

observed_text: QSA takes δ = √(2ρ/ωμ) as the buffer specification. The square root is the diffusion law with D = ρ/μ; that constant is measured and is not derived from a more primitive node count.
implied_text: The spatial buffer is located (classical δ, under a local Ohm's law) but not derived from node rules.
description: Same class of gap as reflection taking λ/4πk: the length is measured, then used as the hardware spec.
notes: File-level mapping remains High.

observed_text: No thickness cutoff accompanies the spectral edge. A continuous 5.66 nm Au film transmits as the bulk-constant calculation predicts, and seeded Au is optically a continuous metal down to 1 nm. Carrier densities that set the edge: Al 1.81e29, Ag 5.86e28, Na 2.65e28 m^-3.
implied_text: The edge is a property of the carrier population and its density. No minimum film thickness is measured; the thickness dependence is a crossover owned by reflection.
description: The spectral edge needs a carrier population, not a minimum connected thickness.
value_text: no minimum thickness measured (continuous Au responds at 5.66 nm and at 1 nm)
notes: The first version carried a 10–20 nm floor and a 5–10 nm cliff inherited from reflection; both withdrawn. The key name is kept for stability.

observed_text: Ionospheric peak layer densities vary between 1e4 and more than 1e6 electrons per cm³ (1e10 to more than 1e12 m^-3), a factor of 5.9e16 to 1.8e18 below the carrier density of Ag or Al.
implied_text: The same clock rule runs in a dilute free-electron column. The hardware is a carrier density that sets a radio-band plasma frequency, not a crystal.
description: Dilute-plasma hardware is a charged column at 1e10–1e12 m^-3, not a metallic film.
notes: value_si is the geometric mean of the quoted range. The first version gave the ratio to a metal as about 1e17.

observed_text: Plasma periods h/E: 0.28 fs (Al, 15.0 eV measured); 0.72 fs (Na, 5.75 eV); 1.1 fs (K, 3.80 eV); Ag 0.46 fs at the free-electron 9.0 eV and 1.1 fs at the measured 3.8 eV. Ionosphere: 1.1 µs at 1e10, 0.35 µs at 1e11, 0.11 µs at 1e12 m^-3.
implied_text: The collective cycle is the plasma period. A drive slower than that is returned; a faster one is not.
description: Clock is load-bearing. The metal cycle is 0.28–1.1 fs; the ionospheric cycle 0.1–1 µs.
notes: value_si is the geometric mean of the metal range. The first version gave the ionospheric cycle as microseconds.

observed_text: Operating condition is a drive below the measured edge: Al 15.0–15.3 eV; Na 5.75 eV; K 3.80 eV; Ag 3.78–3.92 eV. No continuous external power beyond the incident field.
implied_text: Driven collective response, not a memory. ℏωp is an energy scale of the clock, not an activation barrier that holds a state.
description: The window is a clock ceiling, not a latch barrier.
value_text: drive below the edge (Ag: below 3.8–3.9 eV); no latch
notes: Do not identify the Ag edge at 3.8–3.9 eV with the Ag work function, 4.26–4.74 eV (photoelectric-threshold).

observed_text: Reflectance falls above the measured plasmon energy: Al 15.0–15.3 eV (82.7–81.0 nm); Na 5.75 eV; K 3.80 eV. Alkali films become transparent at Cs 440, Rb 360, K 315 and Na 210 nm. Ag: bulk R falls from 95.6 % at 381.5 nm to 5.5 % at 320.4 nm, with a transmission window near 320 nm that interband absorption closes by 301 nm.
implied_text: Drive faster than the collective screening clock and the reflected beam is lost. In a real metal the edge is steep and continuous, with a width set by damping and interband transitions; above it Ag absorbs.
description: This entry owns the spectral edge that reflection also lists. A crossover in a real metal; sharp only in the collisionless model.
value_text: above the edge: Al 15.0–15.3 eV; Ag 3.78–3.92 eV
notes: value_si is the Al plasmon energy over h. Al and Na lie 3–5 % below the free-electron value, K, Rb and Cs 13–18 % below, and Ag at 0.42 of it.

observed_text: Ionospheric peak densities of 1e10 to more than 1e12 m^-3 give plasma frequencies of 1 to more than 9 MHz (0.90, 2.84 and 8.98 MHz at 1e10, 1e11 and 1e12 m^-3). Radio below the plasma frequency of a layer is returned and higher frequencies pass; Faraday rotation is still measured at 100–200 MHz.
implied_text: The same gate in a dilute charged gas: in the collisionless model a wave below f_p does not propagate.
description: The ionosphere is the low-density instance of the same clock failure, and the filed case nearest the collisionless limit.
value_text: f below 1 to above 9 MHz is returned (ionosphere)
notes: value_si is the plasma frequency at 1e12 m^-3. The threshold label rests on the collisionless model; no measured width of the cutoff was opened.

observed_text: Below the edge the metal reflects: a fresh aluminised mirror measures 90.0–91.4 % at 404–624 nm. Above it the alkalis transmit; Ag has a narrow transmission window near 320 nm and is otherwise absorbing.
implied_text: A material-typical plasma or interband edge: high R below, a propagating or absorbed wave above, at zero extra power.
description: The synchronized electron gas emits a spectral gate, not a stored state.
notes: Bound-charge analogue of ω≫ωp is refraction-dielectric’s ε→1 X-ray limit.

observed_text: ωp = √(ne²/ε₀m) gives 15.8 eV for Al and 6.04 eV for Na against measured 15.0–15.3 and 5.75 eV, and lies 13–18 % above the measured value in K, Rb and Cs. For Ag it gives 8.99 eV against a measured 3.78 eV.
implied_text: QSA takes the measured edge as the clock specification. It does not derive the period from a more primitive node update, and the free-electron formula needs a material-specific screening correction.
description: Same class of gap as reflection taking λ/4πk as the decay length. Not a contradiction.
value_text: edge taken, not derived; ωp(n) needs a screening correction
notes: File-level mapping remains High. Contrast photoelectric-threshold: collective carrier density against a single-electron work function.

observed_text: Kretschmann measurements on 30, 52 and 70 nm gold found about 50 nm appropriate. Computed minimum p-polarised reflectance at 633 nm on a 1.515 prism: Au 6 % at 40 nm, 0.9 % at 45 nm, 0.6 % at 50 nm, 15 % at 60 nm; Ag 2.9 % at 50 nm, 1.0 % at 55 nm. Gold–dielectric composite films give the sharp dip only above a metal fill fraction of about 0.6 and no surface mode below about 0.4.
implied_text: Three spatial resources: a metal–dielectric interface, a thickness inside the coupler window, and enough metal in the plane. The window is not a universal 50 nm law.
description: SPR hardware is an interface, a thickness window and a metal fill fraction.
value_text: 45–55 nm (Au and Ag at 633 nm; Kretschmann window)
notes: The centre of the window moves with metal, wavelength and coupler (Au at 550 nm: near 40 nm). The first version contrasted this with a 10–20 nm mirror floor, which does not exist. Localized particle resonance is a different spatial resource.

observed_text: Computed from the single-interface dispersion relation with tabulated n and k at 450–633 nm: field 1/e depth 22–35 nm in the metal and 0.28–0.67 of a wavelength (176–423 nm) in air or water. Run along the surface at 633 nm: 65–73 µm on Ag–air, 25 µm on Ag–water, 9.8–15 µm on Au–air.
implied_text: The dielectric-side evanescent tail is an additional buffer. A coupler (prism index plus angle, or a grating period) is part of the hardware even though it is not the electron gas.
description: SPR occupies a sub-wavelength dielectric tail plus tens of nanometres of metal.
value_text: dielectric tail 0.3–0.7 λ; metal depth 22–35 nm
notes: Model values from measured optical constants; no direct measurement of a propagation length was opened. The run length is not the thickness window.

observed_text: A surface plasmon resonance requires the real part of the metal permittivity to be negative and larger in magnitude than its imaginary part and the permittivity of the adjoining medium, which holds below the interband-screened edge of the metal.
implied_text: Optical-cycle synchronization of the same free-electron gas. Above the edge the bound mode no longer exists.
description: SPR shares reflection’s femtosecond screening clock; the new constraint is momentum, not a new cycle time.
notes: Cross-cite reflection:clock_latency:plasma-period and plasma-frequency-cutoff for the periods (0.28–1.1 fs). This file does not restate them.

observed_text: No stored state. The dip exists only while the film is driven through a coupler.
implied_text: No static barrier holds the dip. The mode exists only while it is driven.
description: SPR is a driven interface mode, not a stored directional state.

observed_text: The wavevector of the surface mode exceeds that of light in the adjoining dielectric, so a free-space photon cannot couple to it directly. A prism in attenuated total reflection (Kretschmann or Otto) or a grating supplies the difference.
implied_text: No in-plane momentum match → the interface mode is not launched → no dip.
description: Momentum match is load-bearing hardware and the primary collapse when the coupler or angle is absent.
value_text: no coupler, or θ / grating off the match
notes: total-internal-reflection supplies the prism evanescent field that Kretschmann and Otto use. Shared hardware, not a shared collapse.

observed_text: Computed minimum reflectance for Au at 633 nm goes from 6 % at 40 nm through 0.6 % at 50 nm to 15 % at 60 nm. In gold–dielectric composite films the dip is sharp above a metal fill fraction of about 0.6, very broad between about 0.4 and 0.6, and absent below about 0.4.
implied_text: Thickness off the window weakens the dip continuously. A granular film keeps a broadened dip until the metal fill falls below about 0.4.
description: Spatial failure is a window in thickness and a set of regimes in metal fill, both crossovers.
value_text: window about 45–55 nm (Au and Ag, 633 nm); fill fraction 0.4–0.6
notes: The first version listed a discontinuous morphology as killing the mode and compared the window with a 5–10 nm reflection cliff. The measured result is three regimes by fill fraction (Shi et al. 2009), and reflection has no such cliff.

observed_text: A narrow dip appears in reflected intensity as angle or wavelength is scanned; the computed minimum is 0.6 % for 50 nm Au at 633 nm. The dip moves when the refractive index of the medium against the metal changes.
implied_text: A sharp angular or spectral absorption feature and a field bound to the interface, from synchronized oscillation of the metal electrons against the dielectric.
description: The stable output is the resonance dip and the interface-bound field, not a bulk mirror R.
notes: No universal minimum reflectance is quoted; the figure is for one film and wavelength.

observed_text: A momentum-matching coupler is required. The coupler is a wavevector match, not a buffer, clock, barrier, lattice, field threshold, or thermal limit.
implied_text: The load-bearing wavevector match does not sit in the six allowed constraint tags. The thickness window and the fill-fraction regimes are also not a single buffer number.
description: Tag-set gap plus a moving window: Medium mapping, not a contradiction of the electron-gas family.
value_text: k-match outside tag set; window and regimes, no floor
notes: File-level mapping remains Medium. Do not invent a seventh tag for one entry.

observed_text: An evanescent field occupies the low-index side. Amplitude decay length 1/κ = λ0 / (2π √(n1² sin²θ − n2²)), which diverges at θc. Glass/air (n1 = 1.50): 0.19 λ0 at 60°, 0.45 λ0 at 45°, 1.85 λ0 at 42°.
implied_text: An interface between two polarizable populations with n1>n2, plus a far-side buffer of order 1/κ. Same bound-charge machines as refraction-dielectric, not a new species.
description: TIR hardware is index contrast plus a wavelength-scale evanescent volume.
value_text: 1/κ ≈ 0.2 λ0 to a few λ0, diverging at θc
notes: A third medium inside the tail takes light out (frustrated TIR); that dependence on gap is continuous. Formula read on a tertiary page.

observed_text: Clock is the optical period. TIR works across the transparency window of the two dielectrics.
implied_text: Clock is not the load-bearing specification. The gate works wherever the two media are transparent and n1 > n2, and fails where the index contrast does — a failure of the underlying refraction machines.
description: TIR inherits the optical cycle of refraction; the collapse is geometric, not temporal.
notes: Cross-cite refraction-dielectric:clock_latency:optical-cycle (~2 fs visible) for the parent cycle time.

observed_text: Time-averaged Poynting flux through the interface is zero in lossless TIR. Energy still occupies the evanescent volume.
implied_text: Driven boundary response, not a latch. The word barrier for the low-index gap in frustrated TIR is a wave-tunneling metaphor, not an energy-barrier tag.
description: No stored state and no activation barrier. The gap is a spatial buffer.
value_text: no latch; evanescent gap is not ΔE

observed_text: θc = arcsin(n2/n1). Against air: glass (n1 = 1.50) 41.8°; water (1.333) 48.6°; polystyrene (1.49) 42.2°; diamond (2.42) 24.4°. For θ<θc a propagating transmitted beam appears and R<1.
implied_text: Incidence below the geometric gate → the total-reflection output is gone.
description: The load-bearing geometric collapse is θ<θc.
notes: value_si is 41.8° in radians, glass/air. Water 48.6°, diamond 24.4°. The condition is θ<θc, not a universal angle; it is sharp for a plane wave in lossless media. Metal reflection gives high R without any critical angle.

observed_text: No real θc exists if n1≤n2.
implied_text: Without index contrast the geometry gate never opens.
description: n1≤n2 is a binary contrast condition.
notes: Total internal reflection occurs only when the second medium has the lower index.

observed_text: A third medium brought within a few wavelengths of the surface receives a transmitted wave, and transmission rises as the gap narrows. No change in θ or in n1, n2 is needed.
implied_text: A third body in the 1/κ buffer takes light out of the reflected beam; the loss grows continuously as the gap narrows.
description: Frustrated TIR is a crossover in gap width, roughly e^(−2κg).
value_text: third body within ~1/κ (0.2 λ0 to a few λ0); continuous in gap
notes: surface-plasmon-resonance uses this tail as a coupler rather than as a collapse.

observed_text: Fresnel reflection coefficients have magnitude 1 (lossless media) for θ>θc, with an angle- and polarization-dependent phase.
implied_text: Unit reflectance for all θ>θc, together with a non-propagating field occupying a wavelength-scale volume on the far side.
description: The synchronized boundary response emits R=1 (lossless) and an evanescent occupancy, without a metal electron gas.
notes: Absorption in either medium → |r|<1 even above θc.

observed_text: The six allowed tags have no slot for angle or index contrast. spatial-buffer covers the interface, the evanescent tail, and frustrated-TIR starvation. It does not name the critical-angle gate.
implied_text: The θc / n1>n2 conditions are recorded as a geometry/contrast gate but are not a first-class constraint tag.
description: Limitation of the tag list, not a reason to invent a tag for one file. Mapping still rates High because two failure modes are sharp.
notes: File-level mapping remains High. Not a new collective oscillator; kinematic gate on refraction’s n.

observed_text: Path for a 45° rotation at 1 T: 6.0 mm of TGG at 632 nm, 2.1 cm of TGG at 1064 nm, 21 cm of fused silica at 633 nm. The interstellar case uses parsecs of dilute plasma. The rotation is proportional to L and has no minimum length.
implied_text: The buffer is the path L through a magneto-optically active population (bound charges with a magnetic splitting, or a magnetized plasma), not a film thickness.
description: Faraday hardware is a path budget.
notes: value_si is the TGG path for 45° at 1 T and 1064 nm, not a minimum. Silica needs about 21 cm; interstellar RM uses parsecs.

observed_text: V is quoted at 632–633 nm and 1064 nm. Cold-plasma Faraday rotation (ω≫ωc, ωp) goes as 1/ω², i.e. λ²; it is measured at about 100–200 MHz, 11–200 times the ionospheric plasma frequency of 1–9 MHz.
implied_text: The carrier is optical or radio. In a plasma the carrier must be above the plasma frequency for the wave to propagate; above it the rotation fades as 1/ω² and does not stop at the edge.
description: Clock is the carrier; the load-bearing resource is the VBL product, not a cycle time.
value_text: optical / radio carrier; plasma rotation ∝ λ² above ωp
notes: Cross-cite cyclotron-resonance: resonant absorption at ω=ωc. Do not file the two as one artifact.

observed_text: θ = VBL in the linear regime. θ∝B through zero. Non-reciprocity: two passes through the same B double θ.
implied_text: No latch. B is a load-bearing resource, not a gate with a finite onset. Tag field-threshold marks that resource, not a step-function threshold.
description: Faraday has a field resource, not an energy barrier that stores a written polarization.
value_text: θ ∝ B through zero; no latch
notes: Tesla-scale B is the laboratory class, not an onset.

observed_text: With B→0 the rotation is gone.
implied_text: Field under-provisioning sends θ→0 linearly. There is no finite onset field.
description: B→0 is a linear fade, θ ∝ B.

observed_text: θ = VBL is linear in L. The rotation falls below a given polarimetric floor when the product VBL does. Absorption limits the usable L.
implied_text: Path below the VBL detection budget → no measurable rotation. A slightly short path is a smaller angle, not a disappeared machine.
description: Spatial failure is a detection budget, linear in L.
notes: Product of V, B and L; no minimum length, so value_si is null. Opacity is a second path failure with no filed scale.

observed_text: TGG's V falls from −131 to −38 rad T^{-1} m^{-1} between 632 and 1064 nm and rises toward cryogenic temperatures. In a plasma the rotation goes as λ²: a factor of 4 less per doubling of frequency.
implied_text: The coupling per unit path falls continuously with wavelength (dielectric), frequency (plasma) or rising temperature (paramagnetic medium).
description: A zero-V medium is a Faraday path with no accumulator.
value_text: V falls with λ (TGG), with T (paramagnet); plasma rotation ∝ λ²
notes: Cross-cite curie-paramagnetism for the moment ensemble behind paramagnetic V(T); no functional form filed.

observed_text: TGG: −131 to −134 rad T^{-1} m^{-1} at 632 nm, −38 at 1064 nm. Fused silica: 3.7 rad T^{-1} m^{-1} at 633 nm. A double pass doubles the rotation.
implied_text: A rotation angle linear in B and L, non-reciprocal, with a material- and frequency-specific V (or an RM in the plasma case).
description: The synchronized magneto-optical population emits θ=VBL, not a latched moment.
notes: Per-tesla Verdet; value_si left null. Plasma form ψ = ψ0 + RM λ² with RM = 0.81∫ n_e B_∥ dl, measured at 100–200 MHz, far above the plasma frequency. TGG values are from tertiary pages, silica from a secondary citation.

observed_text: The mapping takes V as measured and does not derive TGG's value. The 0.81 RM prefactor follows from e, m_e, c and ε0 in the cold-plasma model.
implied_text: The magneto-optical coupling is located as a measured path coefficient, not derived.
description: V is taken. Combined with crossover-only failure modes, that keeps the mapping Medium.
notes: Paramagnetic V(T) touches curie-paramagnetism; the Faraday output is a path integral, not a susceptibility reading.

observed_text: A well-resolved line needs ωc τ ≫ 1, equivalently μB ≫ 1. ωc τ = 1 at 1 T needs τ = 5.7 ps (free electron) or 0.38 ps (GaAs), i.e. a mobility of 10⁴ cm² V^{-1} s^{-1}.
implied_text: The quantity that gates the line is the scattering time against the orbit period — a clock resource. No film-thickness specification.
description: Hardware is a carrier population whose scattering time lets an orbit be a well-defined clock.
notes: Si/Ge resonances were recorded near 4 K, but low temperature is one route only: a 100 cm²/(V s) film gives a resolved line above 100 T, one at 295 K.

observed_text: In metals the line is seen below the plasma frequency with B parallel to the surface. The field occupies a thin skin layer; carriers accelerated there orbit in the bulk and return to the layer in step with the drive (Azbel'–Kaner resonance).
implied_text: 3D-metal CR adds the skin layer as the only volume the drive occupies. The cyclotron match is a different clock from the skin itself.
description: Metal CR borrows skin-effect’s screening length as its spatial buffer.
value_text: Azbel–Kaner recut of the skin layer
notes: Cross-cite skin-effect.

observed_text: ωc = eB/m*. Free electron: fc/B = 27.99 GHz T^{-1}. GaAs conduction electrons: m* = 0.067 m0, so 0.42 THz T^{-1}. In a two-dimensional sheet the collective line is at ω² = ωp² + ωc².
implied_text: Clock is load-bearing. ω must match ωc. B sets that clock. τ is the reset / decoherence time of the orbital motion.
description: A driven orbital clock at eB/m*, not a plasma-period screening cycle.
notes: si_unit is Hz per tesla; value_si is the 1 T frequency. The spin-resonance value is 28.025 GHz T^{-1}, 0.116 % higher; the two lines are distinct and the degree of freedom here is orbital. Ge transverse 0.34 and Si transverse 0.15 THz T^{-1}.

observed_text: No continuous power is required of the sample beyond the probing field. B sets ωc and raises ωc τ.
implied_text: No latch. field-threshold marks B as a clock-setting resource, not a stored-state barrier.
description: CR is a driven orbital match. There is no barrier holding a written state.

observed_text: Off resonance the absorption falls along a line of width about 1/τ. Only one sense of circular polarization is absorbed.
implied_text: Clock mismatch lowers the absorption continuously over the linewidth.
description: The load-bearing spectral failure is detuning from ωc.
notes: B→0 sends ωc→0 and ωcτ→0 together.

observed_text: With too much scattering the line is not resolved at the matching field. The condition is ωc τ = μB ≫ 1; it is met at 295 K above 100 T in a film with mobility 100 cm² V^{-1} s^{-1} (μB = 1 at 100 T).
implied_text: The orbit is not completed. Temperature acts by shortening τ, and a higher field compensates.
description: Scattering-time failure of the orbital clock. Twin of the ωcτ≳1 hardware spec.
notes: A crossover in μB, not a transition temperature. quantum-hall-effect uses the same high-μB two-dimensional carriers; the output there is a quantized Hall resistance, not an m* line.

observed_text: The resonance field at a known frequency is read as an effective mass. GaAs electrons: m* = 0.067 m0. Ge electrons near 4 K: ml = 1.58, mt = 0.082; Si: ml = 0.97, mt = 0.19 (units of the electron mass).
implied_text: An absorption line whose position is the effective mass (or mass tensor) of the carrier population.
description: The synchronized orbital response emits m* as a measured output, not as a derived node mass.
notes: value_si left null: the file quotes ratios to the electron mass. In a two-dimensional sheet the collective line is shifted by the plasma term and must be corrected before it is read as a mass.

observed_text: The mapping records 0.067 m0 in GaAs as a measured output of the lattice-plus-carrier machine. It does not derive that fraction from node rules.
implied_text: m* is located as an emergent output. The lattice that renormalizes the mass is pointed at, not derived here.
description: Open item is m* itself. Clock match and the ωc τ condition still close as a High mapping.
notes: File-level mapping remains High. CR does not become a lattice-mode entry: the collapse is not a phonon cutoff. Cross-cite semiconductor-gap-absorption and faraday-rotation (off-resonant cousin).

observed_text: Two coherent paths that together enclose a flux. A toroidal magnet shielded by superconductor and copper gave a measured phase shift between a beam through the hole and a beam outside. Submicron gold rings show the same period in their resistance.
implied_text: The loop is the buffer. The solenoid interior is not the electron's hardware.
description: AB needs a multiply connected coherent path around a confined flux.
notes: In a metal ring the field also passes through the metal; the field-free condition belongs to the electron-beam experiment.

observed_text: Loss of phase coherence across the loop removes the oscillation; in gold rings its amplitude depends on temperature.
implied_text: Clock is path coherence, not a plasma period.
description: Loss of phase coherence collapses the AB shift.
notes: No coherence length or time is filed.

observed_text: Enclosed flux sets a phase, Δφ = qΦ/ħ. There is no static barrier holding a latched state.
implied_text: Driven interferometer, not a memory.
description: AB is not a latch.
value_text: no latch; Φ writes a phase

observed_text: A path that does not encircle the flux, or Φ→0, removes the shift.
implied_text: Topology / zero flux is the collapse of this effect.
description: No enclosed flux ⇒ no AB shift.
notes: Topology is a threshold. The dependence on Φ itself is continuous: phase linear in Φ, pattern periodic in h/e.

observed_text: Fringe shift or resistance oscillation periodic in Φ_AB = h/e = 4.135667696e-15 Wb (exact). One period for a 1 µm diameter loop is 5.3 mT.
implied_text: Single-charge flux period, not superconducting h/2e.
description: The stable output is an h/e-periodic phase shift.
notes: Twice the tabulated flux quantum h/2e. Contrast with flux-quantization Φ0=h/2e.

observed_text: The fundamental period in a normal conductor is h/e. Normal-metal rings also show a weaker h/2e component, and the shielded-toroid experiment used a superconductor whose own flux is quantized.
implied_text: Do not fold AB into gapped-condensate or identify the two quanta.
description: h/e versus h/2e is a load-bearing distinction, but both periods can appear in one apparatus.

observed_text: Measured from about 50 nm to 7 µm: 0.1–0.9 µm (atomic force microscope), 0.5–3.0 µm (parallel plates), 0.6–6 µm and 0.7–7 µm (torsion). A 9 nm palladium film and a visibly transparent conducting oxide still give a force.
implied_text: The buffer is the gap (which electromagnetic modes fit). The faces need an electromagnetic contrast; no minimum face thickness is measured.
description: Casimir needs a sub-micrometre to micrometre gap between contrasting faces.
notes: The first version required conducting faces thicker than their screening depth; withdrawn. value_si is the 1 µm class.

observed_text: Characteristic frequency c/2d: ħc/2d is 0.99 eV at 100 nm and 0.10 eV at 1 µm. The force integrates the response of the faces over a wide band around it.
implied_text: Clock is the gap electromagnetic spectrum, far below the plasma edge of the faces.
description: Mode spectrum of the gap, not ωp of the faces.

observed_text: The force is a geometry output of the mode spectrum. No stored bit.
implied_text: Not a latch.
description: Casimir is not a memory.

observed_text: The ideal force falls as 1/d⁴ for plates and 1/d³ for a sphere and plate. It has been measured out to 6–7 µm; above about 3 µm at 300 K the thermal contribution dominates.
implied_text: Opening the gap lowers the output continuously.
description: A power law in d with no critical gap.
notes: value_si is the largest gap at which the force has been measured; there is no critical gap.

observed_text: Ideal plate pressure π²ħc/240d⁴ = 1.30 mPa at d = 1 µm (K_C = 1.300e-27 N m²). Measured K_C = (1.22 ± 0.18)e-27 N m² at 0.5–3.0 µm. Thick real metals give 0.48–0.55 of the ideal force at 0.1 µm.
implied_text: Taken mode-sum output, not derived from a node count; real faces reduce it continuously.
description: The stable output is the Casimir/Lifshitz attraction.
notes: value_si is the ideal 1 µm plate pressure.

observed_text: The π²ħc/240 prefactor is taken from the mode sum. Real faces reduce the force through their measured dielectric response; roughness and patch potentials also sit between the formula and any one apparatus.
implied_text: Same class of taken output as the optical decay length λ/4πk.
description: Prefactor taken; mapping Medium.
